avoid_supplements.name: Aspirin or other salicylates
avoid_supplements.mechanism: Additive salicylate exposure increases risk of salicylism, tinnitus, and bleeding complications
avoid_supplements.action: Avoid concurrent use; separate dosing by at least 2 hours if necessary

avoid_supplements.name: Warfarin or other anticoagulants
avoid_supplements.mechanism: Bismuth subsalicylate's salicylate component inhibits platelet aggregation and may potentiate anticoagulant effects
avoid_supplements.action: Monitor INR closely; consider alternative antidiarrheal agent

avoid_supplements.name: High-dose vitamin K supplements
avoid_supplements.mechanism: May antagonize the antiplatelet effects of salicylate component
avoid_supplements.action: Maintain consistent vitamin K intake; avoid sudden increases

caution_supplements.name: NSAIDs (ibuprofen, naproxen)
caution_supplements.mechanism: Additive GI irritation and increased bleeding risk due to salicylate component
caution_supplements.action: Use lowest effective dose and monitor for GI symptoms

caution_supplements.name: Probiotics
caution_supplements.mechanism: Bismuth may have antimicrobial effects that could affect probiotic efficacy

avoid_foods.name: Alcohol
avoid_foods.mechanism: Increases GI irritation and bleeding risk; enhances salicylate absorption and toxicity
avoid_foods.action: Avoid alcohol consumption during bismuth subsalicylate therapy

caution_foods.name: High-salicylate foods (berries, tomatoes, peppers, nuts)
caution_foods.mechanism: Cumulative salicylate intake may increase risk of adverse effects in sensitive individuals
caution_foods.action: Monitor for signs of salicylism; no strict avoidance needed for most patients

caution_foods.name: Dairy products
caution_foods.mechanism: May reduce bismuth subsalicylate absorption when consumed simultaneously
caution_foods.action: Separate dairy consumption by at least 2 hours from medication

monitoring_notes: Monitor for signs of salicylism (tinnitus, dizziness, altered mental status) especially with prolonged use or in patients >60 years. Black/dark stools are expected and benign; however, monitor for GI bleeding signs in patients on concurrent anticoagulants or antiplatelets.
